rooms.name: Alphabet & pronunciation hall [first floor 1] · letters A–M
rooms.setting: Alphabet & pronunciation hall inside Petite École (first schoolhouse).
grammar_rules: 26 letters; names differ from English (e = 'euh', i = 'ee', g = 'zhay', j = 'zhee', r = 'air', u = 'ew').
Accents: é (aigu), è à ù (grave), ê â î ô û (circonflexe), ë ï ü (tréma), ç (cédille).
Final consonants are usually silent, except often C, R, F, L (think 'CaReFuL').
Nasal vowels: an/en [ɑ̃], on [ɔ̃], in/ain/ein [ɛ̃], un [œ̃].
The French R is made at the back of the throat [ʁ].
U [y] = say 'ee' with rounded lips; OU [u] = English 'oo'.
H is always silent; 'h aspiré' words block elision and liaison (le haricot).

rooms.name: Grammar rules I (gender, articles, plural)
rooms.setting: Grammar rules I (gender, articles, plural) inside Petite École (first schoolhouse).
grammar_rules: Every noun is masculine or feminine; learn the article with the noun (here: feminine LEFT, masculine RIGHT).
Definite articles: le (m), la (f), l' (before a vowel or mute h), les (plural).
Indefinite articles: un (m), une (f), des (plural).
Partitive articles: du (m), de la (f), de l' (vowel), des — 'some' (du pain, de l'eau).
After a negation, un/une/du/de la/des become de/d' (je n'ai pas de pain).
Plural: usually add -s (silent); -eau/-eu add -x; -al often becomes -aux; -s/-x/-z do not change.
Adjectives agree in gender and number: petit, petite, petits, petites.
Most adjectives follow the noun; BAGS adjectives (Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size) usually precede it.
Contractions: à + le = au, à + les = aux, de + le = du, de + les = des.

rooms.name: Grammar rules II (verbs, negation, questions)
rooms.setting: Grammar rules II (verbs, negation, questions) inside Petite École (first schoolhouse).
grammar_rules: Infinitive endings: -er (1st group), -ir with -issons (2nd group), everything else (3rd group, mostly irregular).
Present of -er verbs: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent.
Negation wraps the verb: ne … pas (je ne parle pas); also ne … jamais / plus / rien / personne.
Three ways to ask: intonation (Tu viens ?), est-ce que (Est-ce que tu viens ?), inversion (Viens-tu ?).
Passé composé = avoir/être + past participle; être is used for the 'house of être' movement verbs and all pronominal verbs.
With être, the past participle agrees with the subject (elle est partie).
Pronominal verbs carry a reflexive pronoun: je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève (mirror on the facade).
Near future: aller + infinitive (je vais manger). Recent past: venir de + infinitive (je viens de manger).

rooms.name: General rules (elision, liaison, accents, tu/vous)
rooms.setting: General rules (elision, liaison, accents, tu/vous) inside Petite École (first schoolhouse).
grammar_rules: Elision: le, la, je, me, te, se, ne, de, que drop their vowel before a vowel or mute h (l'ami, j'aime).
Liaison: a normally silent final consonant is pronounced before a vowel (les‿amis [lezami]).
Tu is informal (family, friends, children); vous is formal or plural.
Capital letters are NOT used for days, months, languages or nationality adjectives (lundi, janvier, français).
Punctuation: a space goes before ? ! : ; and inside « guillemets ».
Word order of object pronouns: me/te/se/nous/vous > le/la/les > lui/leur > y > en.
Numbers: 70 = soixante-dix (60+10), 80 = quatre-vingts (4×20), 90 = quatre-vingt-dix.
